objects.why: Represents the myth of sudden epiphany versus engineered insight.
Represents the 20% consumption rule, structured sketches, and written formulas.
Represents modern digital tools, rapid iteration, and prototyping.
Represents the delicate 90/10 equilibrium between familiar security and novel excitement.
Represents finding the exact peak sweet spot of the Creative Curve.

spine.claim: Shattering the myth of divine inspiration by examining how historical hits like Mozart were meticulously engineered.
Unpacking the Creative Curve: the biological conflict between neophilia and neophobia that defines cultural taste.
The Four Laws in practice: consumption (20% rule), imitation of proven structures, and creative network dynamics.
Testing ideas via rapid iteration and data feedback loops to prevent falling into the downslope of creative cliché.
Creativity is an accessible, disciplined craft of timing and soil cultivation, not a rare lightning strike.
